findings.summary: Trained on the grid regenerated with the discontinuous-conduction converter at 1000 substeps (dc_converter_model='dcm', S21-2), i.e. without the S-21 converter artifact: AI-N27 option 2. Same recipe and same train/val/test split as rpi5_resnet1d_se_5class_w2048/2026-10-20_run01, which it replaces. Promoted 2026-11-04 after a pre-registered evaluation (RPi5 (float16 TFLite)): macro-F1 0.925 on the dcm test split (previous model 0.870), 0.924 on held-out runs in the affected regime, 0.980 on the regenerated generalization set.

AI-N27 (mitigated for this run) / S-21: this model was trained without the converter artifact. The production DC plant (dc_perm_ex_v1, the GUI and assistant default) still uses GEM's converter, so its simulations in braking at light load (mostly 80-125 rad/s, high severity) still contain the artifact; on such inputs this model sees a signal it was not trained on. Not measured on GEM-plant inputs beyond the AI-N27 impact study.
2048-sample (205 ms) windows: start-up (t < 0.5 s) macro-F1 0.594 with abstention 0.60 on the held-out runs, 0.467 on the generalization start-up condition; steady state 0.99-1.00.
Lowest per-class recall on the dcm test split: outer_race 0.883 (it fell 2.5-4.2 points vs the previous model, within the pre-registered 5-point margin).
Trained and evaluated on simulated data only (speed x severity x noise x plant-drift grid, DC plant with dcm x1000); no real-machine validation exists.
The float16 model.tflite has never been executed on a Raspberry Pi 5: parity and latency were measured on the development host only.

ball/cage: synthetic-only, uncalibrated amplitude. The ball and cage classes were trained on simulated faults whose mechanical amplitude (CALIBRATED_MECHANICAL_SEVERITY in datagen/scenario.py) is a placeholder: KAt has no clean single-defect code for these faults, so it cannot be calibrated without real data.
